## Precalculus review

[Download the precalculus worksheet](../downloads/precalculus-review-worksheet.pdf){.start-link}

Four pages with 12 problems on functions, domains, graphs, slope, trigonometry, inverses, exponentials, and logarithms.

The numbered topics in [Appendix A: Precalculus review](../lectures/00-functions.qmd) follow this worksheet, using different values for the discussion examples. The [review lecture PDF](../downloads/september-25-chapter-1-review.pdf) is also available.

## Week 2 · Limits

[Download the Week 2 worksheet](../downloads/week-2-worksheet.pdf){.start-link}

Four pages with two investigations:

- **A tangent line on the unit circle:** follow its horizontal intercept as the point of tangency moves toward the top of the circle.
- **When can a graph mislead us?** Compare graphical evidence, exact values, a change of scale, and limit laws.

Related notes: [Limits](../lectures/02-limits.qmd), [Infinite limits](../lectures/03-infinite-limits.qmd), and [Limit laws](../lectures/04-limit-laws.qmd).

**Note on page 4.** The original PDF is preserved as distributed. Its final physical-scale aside is inaccurate: approximately $1.6\times10^{-35}$ meters is the *Planck length* ([NIST](https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/codata.pdf)). The “10 billion times” comparison should be disregarded. For this function, the relevant horizontal scale is $10^{-1013}$, as in part (c), because $(10^{-1013})^2=10^{-2026}$. The graph's coordinates have no physical units unless a scale is explicitly assigned.

## Week 4 · Derivatives {#week-4-derivatives}

[Download the Week 4 worksheet](../downloads/week-4-worksheet.pdf){.start-link}

Four pages with two investigations:

- **Problem 1. A tangent line and a limiting area** — Monday, Sections 3.1–3.2. Use the derivative definition for $f(x)=1/x$, find tangent-line intercepts, and investigate the triangle's area and perimeter as $a\to0^+$.
- **Problem 2. Is the fish population recovering?** — Wednesday, Sections 3.3–3.4. Interpret the graph of a population's rate of change, sketch the population, and consider possible future fishing restrictions.

Related notes: [The derivative at a point](../lectures/09-derivative-at-a-point.qmd) and [The derivative function](../lectures/10-derivative-function.qmd).
